title: What key makes a pictograph of the dogs?
description: The Mudhol hounds of six villages are shown as a pictograph. A key of one symbol for six dogs is chosen because every count is a multiple of six, the symbols of Village B are counted, and two villages together are compared with the other four.
teaching_notes: One idea: choose a key that divides all the counts, so the pictograph stays short, and then compare totals by adding the counts. Watch for students who pick a key of one symbol for one dog and run out of room.

video_script.why: The child chooses a key for a pictograph of large counts, counts the symbols of one village, and compares two villages with the rest.
video_script.substitution: The Mudhol hounds in six villages are drawn with a key of one symbol for several dogs.
video_script.anchor: a table of the Mudhol hounds in six villages, ready to be drawn as a pictograph
video_script.payoff_line: One symbol stands for six dogs, Village B needs six symbols, and the child is right

final_answer.value: a. 1 symbol = 6 dogs; b. 6 symbols; c. Yes, B + D = 84, more than the other four villages, 72
final_answer.spoken: one symbol stands for six dogs, Village B needs six symbols, and yes, the child is right

maths_rules: dogs: Village A 18, Village B 36, Village C 12, Village D 48, Village E 18, Village F 24
every count is a multiple of 6: 18 = 3 x 6, 36 = 6 x 6, 12 = 2 x 6, 48 = 8 x 6, 18 = 3 x 6, 24 = 4 x 6
key: 1 symbol = 6 dogs; one symbol for one dog would need 48 symbols for Village D
symbols: Village A 3, Village B 6, Village C 2, Village D 8, Village E 3, Village F 4
Village B and Village D together: 36 + 48 = 84
84 is more than 72, so the child is right
check by symbols: 6 + 8 = 14, and 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 12, and 14 is more than 12
video_script.design: The counts of the six villages are written in a table, and a key is chosen by seeing that each count is a multiple of six. The symbols are counted, and the two totals are compared in dogs and again in symbols.
